title: Which Zscaler API reads return secrets: scoping a read-only API client

prose.text: A role that can only read can still be given credential material, because some read operations return it. This walks the read surfaces by what they return: the secret itself, a masked value, or nothing.

prose.label: Reads that return a secret.
prose.text: Provisioning keys, ZTW API keys and provisioning URLs, ZCC device passwords and OTPs, and the ZPA objects whose read schemas list private keys or passwords are in [[shared.secret-surfaces.revealed]].

prose.label: Reads that withhold it.
prose.text: The ZIA admin password, the Sandbox submission token, the ZIA cloud service API key, ZIdentity API client secrets and Browser Access certificate keys are in [[shared.secret-surfaces.withheld]].

prose.label: Terraform state.
prose.text: A secret read back by a Terraform provider is written to state whether or not the attribute is marked sensitive: [[zpa.app-connectors.provisioning-key-tooling:provider-stores-key-in-state]]; the wider picture is [[shared.terraform.credential-handling]].

checks.do: Whether a read-only API client or role can reach ZPA provisioning keys, which return the enrollment key in the read.
Whether it can reach ZTW API keys or provisioning URLs.
Whether it can reach the ZCC OTP and password reads, which return the values that uninstall or disable Client Connector.

Whether it can reach ZPA PRA credentials, enrollment certificates, API keys or ZIA VPN credentials, whose live read behavior is unverified, and treat them as secret-bearing until a read shows otherwise.
Whether Terraform state for these resources is stored as a secret.
